units.zh: 到仲舉 韓子高 華皎
units.en: Dao Zhongju; Han Zigao; Hua Jiao
units.literal: Dao Zhongju; Han Zigao; Hua Jiao

units.zh: 到仲舉字德言，彭城武原人也。
units.en: Dao Zhongju, styled Deyan, came from Wuyuan in Pengcheng.
units.literal: Dao Zhongju, styled Deyan, was a native of Wuyuan in Pengcheng.

units.zh: 祖坦，齊中書侍郎。
units.en: His grandfather Tan had been Qi’s secretariat attendant.
units.literal: His grandfather Tan was Secretariat Attendant of Qi.

units.zh: 父洽，梁侍中。
units.en: His father Qia was a palace attendant under Liang.
units.literal: His father Qia was Palace Attendant of Liang.

units.zh: 仲舉無他藝業，而立身耿正。
units.en: Zhongju had no special craft, but he stood upright in his conduct.
units.literal: Zhongju had no other art or profession, yet in establishing himself he was upright and steadfast.

units.zh: 釋褐著作佐郎、太子舍人、王府主簿。
units.en: He entered service as editorial officer of writings, palace gentleman in attendance, and chief clerk of a princely establishment.
units.literal: He doffed the commoner's garb as Editorial Officer of Writings, Palace Gentleman in Attendance, and Chief Clerk of the Prince's establishment.

units.zh: 出為長城令，政號廉平。
units.en: Posted as magistrate of Changcheng, he won a name for honest, even rule.
units.literal: He went out as magistrate of Changcheng; his governance was famed for integrity and fairness.

units.zh: 文帝居鄉里，嘗詣仲舉，時天陰雨，仲舉獨坐齋內，聞城外有簫鼓之聲，俄而文帝至，仲舉異之，乃深自結託。
units.en: While Emperor Wen was still in the countryside he once called on Zhongju. Rain fell under a leaden sky. Zhongju sat alone in his study and heard flutes and drums beyond the wall. Then Emperor Wen arrived. Struck by the omen, Zhongju gave him his deepest trust.
units.literal: When Emperor Wen was in the countryside, he once visited Zhongju. The sky was cloudy and rainy; Zhongju sat alone in his study and heard outside the walls the sound of flutes and drums. Presently Emperor Wen arrived. Zhongju thought it strange and thereafter bound himself to him in deep trust.

units.zh: 文帝又嘗因飲，夜宿仲舉帳中，忽有神光五采照于室內，由是祇承益恭。
units.en: Emperor Wen once spent the night in Zhongju’s tent after wine. A five-colored light suddenly filled the room. From then on Zhongju served him with still greater reverence.
units.literal: Emperor Wen once lodged in Zhongju's tent after drinking by night. Suddenly a divine light of five colors shone within the room; from this his reverent service grew still more deferential.

units.zh: 侯景之亂，仲舉依文帝。
units.en: When Hou Jing rebelled, Zhongju cast his lot with Emperor Wen.
units.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Zhongju attached himself to Emperor Wen.

units.zh: 及景平，文帝為吳興郡守，以仲舉為郡丞，與潁川庾持俱為文帝賓客。
units.en: After Jing fell, Emperor Wen became administrator of Wu Commandery and made Zhongju his deputy. He and Yu Chi of Yingchuan both served as Emperor Wen’s clients.
units.literal: When Jing was pacified, Emperor Wen became administrator of Wu Commandery and made Zhongju deputy administrator; together with Yu Chi of Yingchuan they were both Emperor Wen's clients.

units.zh: 文帝為宣毅將軍，以仲舉為長史，尋帶山陰令。
units.en: When Emperor Wen was made general who displays martial resolution, he named Zhongju chief clerk and soon gave him the magistracy of Shanyin as well.
units.literal: When Emperor Wen was General Who Displays Martial Resolution, he made Zhongju chief clerk; soon he also held concurrently the magistracy of Shanyin.

units.zh: 文帝嗣位，授侍中，參掌選事。
units.en: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Zhongju was made palace attendant and helped manage appointments.
units.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, [Zhongju] was appointed Palace Attendant and took part in managing selection affairs.

units.zh: 天嘉元年，守都官尚書，封寶安縣侯，邑五百戶。
units.en: In the first year of Tianjia (560) he was made acting minister of the masters of writing for officials and enfeoffed as Marquis of Bao’an with five hundred households.
units.literal: In the first year of Tianjia, he was made acting Minister of the Masters of Writing for Officials, enfeoffed Marquis of Bao'an county with a fief of five hundred households.

units.zh: 三年，除都官尚書。
units.en: In the third year he was appointed minister of the masters of writing for officials.
units.literal: In the third year he was appointed Minister of the Masters of Writing for Officials.

units.zh: 其年，遷尚書右僕射、丹陽尹，參掌並如故。
units.en: That year he was made right vice director of the masters of writing and metropolitan governor of Danyang, with the same role in government as before.
units.literal: That year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing (right) and Metropolitan Governor of Danyang; his participation in government remained as before.

units.zh: 尋改封建昌縣侯。
units.en: Soon his title was changed to Marquis of Jianchang.
units.literal: Soon his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Jianchang county.

units.zh: 仲舉既無學術，朝章非所長，選舉引用，皆出自袁樞。
units.en: Zhongju had no learning and court law was not his field. Every appointment came from Yuan Shu.
units.literal: Zhongju had no learning or scholarship; court regulations were not his strength—all selections and appointments issued from Yuan Shu.

units.zh: 性疏簡，不干涉世務，與朝士無所親狎，但聚財酣飲而已。
units.en: He was spare by nature, kept out of public business, and was close to no courtier. He only hoarded money and drank.
units.literal: By nature he was spare and simple, did not meddle in worldly affairs, and was intimate with no court officials; he merely amassed wealth and drank deep—that was all.

units.zh: 六年，秩滿，解尹。
units.en: In the sixth year his term ended and he left the metropolitan governorship.
units.literal: In the sixth year his term expired and he was relieved of the metropolitan governorship.

units.zh: 是時，文帝積年寢疾，不親御萬機，尚書中事，皆使仲舉斷決。
units.en: By then Emperor Wen had lain ill for years and no longer ran the realm himself. Everything in the masters of writing went to Zhongju for decision.
units.literal: At that time Emperor Wen had been bedridden with illness for years and did not personally oversee the myriad affairs of state; matters within the Masters of Writing were all left to Zhongju to decide.

units.zh: 天康元年，遷侍中、尚書僕射，參掌如故。
units.en: In the first year of Tiankang (566) he was made palace attendant and vice director of the masters of writing, with the same powers as before.
units.literal: In the first year of Tiankang, he was transferred to Palace Attendant and Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; his participation in government remained as before.

units.zh: 文帝疾甚，入侍醫藥。
units.en: When Emperor Wen grew desperately ill, Zhongju entered to nurse him with medicine.
units.literal: When Emperor Wen's illness grew grave, [Zhongju] entered to attend him with medicine.

units.zh: 及文帝崩，高宗受遺詔為尚書令入輔，仲舉與左丞王暹、中書舍人劉師知、殷不佞等，以朝望有歸，乃遣不佞矯宣旨遣高宗還東府。
units.en: When Emperor Wen died, Emperor Xuan took the testament as director of the masters of writing and entered to govern. Zhongju, with the left assistant Wang Xian and secretariat attendants Liu Shizhi and Yin Bujiu, judged where the court’s hopes lay and sent Bujiu to forge an edict ordering Emperor Xuan back to the Eastern Mansion.
units.literal: When Emperor Wen died, Emperor Xuan received the testamentary edict as Director of the Masters of Writing and entered to assist in government. Zhongju, together with Left Assistant Wang Xian, Secretariat Attendants Liu Shizhi and Yin Bujiu, and others—because public expectation had a direction—then sent Bujiu to counterfeit an imperial order and send Emperor Xuan back to the Eastern Mansion.

units.zh: 事發，師知下北獄賜死，暹、不佞並付治，乃以仲舉為貞毅將軍、金紫光祿大夫。
units.en: When the plot came out, Shizhi was sent to the northern prison and granted death. Xian and Bujiu were handed over for trial. Zhongju was reduced to steadfast-resolution general and grandee with the gold seal and purple ribbon.
units.literal: When the affair was exposed, Shizhi was sent to the northern prison and granted death; Xian and Bujiu were both handed over for prosecution. Then Zhongju was made General of Steadfast Resolution and Grandee with the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

units.zh: 初，仲舉子郁尚文帝妹信義長公主，官至中書侍郎，出為宣城太守，文帝配以士馬，是年遷為南康內史，以國哀未之任。
units.en: Earlier Zhongju’s son Yu had married Emperor Wen’s sister, the Senior Princess of Xinyi. He rose to attendant gentleman of the secretariat, then went out as administrator of Xuancheng, and Emperor Wen gave him troops and horses. That year he was named interior minister of Nankang but had not yet taken office because of the state mourning.
units.literal: Earlier, Zhongju's son Yu had married Emperor Wen's younger sister, Princess Xin'an the Long of Xinyi; he reached the post of Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat, went out as Administrator of Xuancheng; Emperor Wen supplied him with warriors and horses. That year he was transferred to Interior Minister of Nankang; because of the state mourning he had not yet taken up the appointment.

units.zh: 仲舉既廢居私宅，與郁皆不自安。
units.en: Zhongju, dismissed and living at home, and Yu both felt uneasy.
units.literal: Zhongju, having been set aside and living in a private residence, and Yu both felt ill at ease.

units.zh: 時韓子高在都，人馬素盛，郁每乘小輿蒙婦人衣與子高謀。
units.en: Han Zigao was then in the capital with a large following of men and horses. Yu would ride in a small carriage dressed as a woman to plot with him.
units.literal: At that time Han Zigao was in the capital; his men and horses had always been numerous. Yu each time rode in a small carriage, cloaked in women's dress, to plot with Zigao.

units.zh: 子高軍主告言其事，高宗收子高、仲舉及郁並付廷尉。
units.en: One of Zigao’s army commanders reported the affair. Emperor Xuan seized Zigao, Zhongju, and Yu and sent them to the court of trials.
units.literal: Zigao's army commander reported the affair. Emperor Xuan arrested Zigao, Zhongju, and Yu and handed them over to the Court of Trials.

units.zh: 詔曰：「到仲舉庸劣小才，坐叨顯貴，受任前朝，榮寵隆赫，父參王政，子據大邦，禮盛外姻，勢均戚里。
units.en: An edict declared: “Dao Zhongju is a mediocre man raised by luck. The former court heaped rank on him: father in the government, son in a great commandery, affinal honors as grand as kinship, power to match the imperial clan.
units.literal: An edict said: "Dao Zhongju is a mediocre, petty talent who by chance enjoyed high rank; he received office from the former court and glory and favor were lofty and bright—father participating in royal government, son holding a great commandery, ritual grand in affinal kinship, power equal to the imperial clan.

units.zh: 而肆此驕闇，凌慠百司，遏密之初，擅行國政，排黜懿親，欺蔑台羇。
units.en: Yet he grew arrogant and dark, insulting every office. At the start of the mourning silence he seized the government, drove out worthy kin, and mocked the Terrace.
units.literal: Yet he indulged this arrogant darkness, insulted and defied the hundred offices; at the beginning of the mourning silence he usurped state government, expelled worthy kin, and scorned the Terrace posts.

units.zh: 韓子高蕞爾細微，擢自卑末，入參禁衛，委以腹心，蜂蠆有毒，敢行反噬。
units.en: Han Zigao is a nothing raised from the gutter. He entered the palace guard and won the innermost trust, yet like a bee or scorpion he turned to bite.
units.literal: Han Zigao is a trifling, minute man, promoted from the lowest ranks, entered to join the palace guard, entrusted with the innermost confidence—yet the bee and scorpion have poison, and he dared turn to bite.

units.zh: 仲舉、子高，共為表裏，陰構姦謀，密為異計。
units.en: Zhongju and Zigao worked as outer shell and inner core, weaving treason in secret.
units.literal: Zhongju and Zigao, together outer and inner, secretly wove treacherous plots and in secret made separate plans.

units.zh: 安成王朕之叔父，親莫重焉，受命導揚，稟承顧託，以朕沖弱，屬當保祐。
units.en: The Prince of Ancheng is my uncle, the closest of kin. He was charged to guide the state and bear the late emperor’s trust. Because I am young, he should protect me.
units.literal: The Prince of Ancheng is Our uncle; in kinship none is heavier. He received the charge to guide and uplift, inherited the entrusted care; because We are young and weak, he ought to protect and preserve Us.

units.zh: 家國安危，事歸宰輔，伊、周之重，物無異議，將相舊臣，咸知宗仰。
units.en: The realm’s safety belongs to its chief ministers. The weight of Yi and Zhou is beyond dispute. Every old general and minister knows to look to him.
units.literal: The safety of house and state rests with the chief ministers; the weight of Yi and Zhou—no one disputes it; the old ministers among generals and chancellors all know to look up to him as the standard.

units.zh: 而率聚凶徒，欲相掩襲，屯據東城，進逼崇禮，規樹仲舉，以執國權，陵斥司徒，意在專政，潛結黨附，方危社稷。
units.en: Yet they gathered villains for a surprise strike, massed at the Eastern City and pressed Chongli, meant to set up Zhongju and seize power, drive off the minister of works and rule alone, knit secret factions, and were about to endanger the dynasty.
units.literal: Yet they gathered wicked followers, intending a surprise attack; they massed at the Eastern City and pressed upon Chongli, planning to set up Zhongju to seize state power, to drive off the Minister of Works with intent to monopolize government, secretly joining factions and parties, and were about to endanger the altars of state.

units.zh: 賴祖宗之靈，姦謀顯露。
units.en: Thanks to the ancestors’ spirits, the plot came to light.
units.literal: Relying on the spirits of the ancestors, the treacherous plot was exposed.

units.zh: 前上虞令陸昉等具告其事，並有據驗，并剋今月七日，縱其凶謀。
units.en: The former magistrate of Shangyu, Lu Fang, and others laid out the whole affair with proof. They had set the seventh of this month for the crime.
units.literal: The former magistrate of Shangyu, Lu Fang, and others fully reported the affair, and there is corroborating evidence; they fixed the seventh day of this month to carry out their wicked plot.

units.zh: 領軍將軍明徹，左衛將軍、衛尉卿寶安及諸公等，又並知其事。
units.en: Area commander Mingche, left guard general and commandant of the guards Bao’an, and the other dukes knew it as well.
units.literal: Area Commander Mingche, Left Guard General and Commandant of the Guards Bao'an, and the various dukes and others also all knew of the affair.

units.zh: 二三舋跡，彰於朝野，反道背德，事駭聞見。
units.en: Their tracks show in court and country alike. Their treason shocks every eye and ear.
units.literal: Two or three traces are plain in court and countryside; their contrary way and betrayed virtue horrify all who hear and see.

units.zh: 今大憝克殲，罪人斯得，並可收付廷尉，肅正刑書。
units.en: Now the great villain is cut down and the guilty taken. Let all be sent to the court of trials and judged by law.
units.literal: Now the great villain is destroyed and the guilty are caught; all may be taken and handed to the Court of Trials to rectify the penal code.

units.zh: 罪止仲舉父子及子高三人而已，其餘一從曠蕩，並所不問。」
units.en: Guilt ends with Zhongju, his son, and Zigao—three people only. All others are wholly pardoned and will not be questioned.”
units.literal: Guilt stops with Zhongju, father and son, and Zigao—three persons only; the rest are wholly pardoned and will not be questioned."

units.zh: 仲舉及郁並於獄賜死，時年五十一。
units.en: Zhongju and Yu were granted death in prison. He was fifty-one.
units.literal: Zhongju and Yu were both granted death in prison; he was fifty-one years old.

units.zh: 郁諸男女，以帝甥獲免。
units.en: Yu’s sons and daughters were spared as the emperor’s affinal kin.
units.literal: Yu's sons and daughters, as the emperor's affinal kin, were pardoned.

units.zh: 韓子高，會稽山陰人也。
units.en: Han Zigao came from Shanyin in Kuaiji.
units.literal: Han Zigao was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji.

units.zh: 家本微賤。
units.en: His family was very lowborn.
units.literal: His family was originally of very low status.

units.zh: 侯景之亂，寓在京都。
units.en: During Hou Jing’s rebellion he stayed in the capital.
units.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he sojourned in the capital.

units.zh: 景平，文帝出守吳興，子高年十六，為總角，容貌美麗，狀似婦人，於淮渚附部伍寄載欲還鄉，文帝見而問之，曰：「能事我乎？」
units.en: After Jing fell, Emperor Wen went out to hold Wu Commandery. Zigao was sixteen, still wearing the boy’s knot, beautiful as a woman. At Huai Ford he joined a convoy bound home. Emperor Wen saw him and asked, “Will you serve me?”
units.literal: When Jing was pacified Emperor Wen went out to hold Wu Commandery. Zigao was sixteen, in the age of the hair knot; his appearance was beautiful and his bearing like a woman's. At Huai Ford he attached to a convoy wishing to return home. Emperor Wen saw him and asked, "Can you serve me?"

units.zh: 子高許諾。
units.en: Zigao agreed.
units.literal: Zigao agreed.

units.zh: 子高本名蠻子，文帝改名之。
units.en: His name had been Manzi; Emperor Wen renamed him.
units.literal: Zigao's original name was Manzi; Emperor Wen changed his name.

units.zh: 性恭謹，勤於侍奉，恆執備身刀及傳酒炙。
units.en: He was respectful and careful, always at hand with the belt knife, pouring wine and serving roast meat.
units.literal: By nature he was respectful and careful, diligent in service, always holding the belt knife for personal attendance and passing wine and roasted meat.

units.zh: 文帝性急，子高恆會意旨。
units.en: Emperor Wen was quick-tempered; Zigao always read his mind.
units.literal: Emperor Wen was quick-tempered by nature; Zigao always grasped his intent.

units.zh: 及長，稍習騎射，頗有膽決，願為將帥，及平杜龕，配以士卒。
units.en: As he grew he learned riding and archery, showed daring, and wanted to be a commander. When Du Kan fell, he was given troops.
units.literal: When he grew older he gradually learned horsemanship and archery; he had considerable daring and resolution and wished to be a commander; when Du Kan was pacified he was given troops.

units.zh: 文帝甚寵愛之，未嘗離於左右。
units.en: Emperor Wen doted on him and never let him leave his side.
units.literal: Emperor Wen cherished him exceedingly and never let him leave his side.

units.zh: 文帝嘗夢見騎馬登山，路危欲墮，子高推捧而升。
units.en: Emperor Wen once dreamed he rode uphill on a perilous path about to fall. Zigao pushed and lifted him up.
units.literal: Emperor Wen once dreamed he rode a horse up a mountain; the road was perilous and he was about to fall; Zigao pushed and supported him so he ascended.

units.zh: 文帝之討張彪也，沈泰等先降，文帝據有州城，周文育鎮北郭香
units.en: When Emperor Wen campaigned against Zhang Biao, Shen Tai and others had already surrendered. Emperor Wen held the prefectural city, and Zhou Wenyü garrisoned north of the city at Xiang
units.literal: When Emperor Wen campaigned against Zhang Biao, Shen Tai and others had already surrendered; Emperor Wen held the prefectural city, and Zhou Wenyü garrisoned north of the city at Xiang

units.en: (Yan)
units.literal: (Yan)

units.zh: 巖寺。
units.en: Yan Temple.
units.literal: Yan Temple.

units.zh: [1]張彪自剡縣夜還襲城，文帝自北門出，倉卒闇夕，軍人擾亂，文育亦未測文帝所在，唯子高在側，文帝乃遣子高自亂兵中往見文育，反命酬答，於闇中又往慰勞眾軍。
units.en: [1] Zhang Biao returned by night from Shan county to storm the city. Emperor Wen slipped out the north gate. In the sudden dark the troops panicked. Wenyü did not know where Emperor Wen was—only Zigao stood beside him. Emperor Wen sent Zigao through the chaos to Wenyü to bring back his orders, then go again in the dark to steady the army.
units.literal: Zhang Biao returned by night from Shan county to raid the city. Emperor Wen went out through the northern gate. In the sudden rush of dark evening the soldiers were in turmoil; Wenyü too had not yet determined where Emperor Wen was—only Zigao was at his side. Emperor Wen then sent Zigao from amid the disorderly troops to go see Wenyü, return with orders and replies, and in the dark go again to comfort the armies.

units.zh: 文帝散兵稍集，子高引導入文育營，因共立柵。
units.en: Emperor Wen’s scattered men slowly gathered. Zigao led him into Wenyü’s camp and together they threw up palisades.
units.literal: Emperor Wen's scattered troops gradually gathered; Zigao led him into Wenyü's camp, and together they built palisades.

units.zh: 明日，與彪戰，彪將申縉復降[2]，彪奔松山，浙東平。
units.en: The next day they fought Biao. Biao’s general Shen Jin surrendered again. [2] Biao fled to Song mountain and eastern Zhe was pacified.
units.literal: The next day they fought Biao; Biao's general Shen Jin surrendered again Biao fled to Song mountain; eastern Zhe was pacified.

units.zh: 文帝乃分麾下多配子高，子高亦輕財禮士，歸之者甚眾。
units.en: Emperor Wen then gave Zigao many of his own followers. Zigao was generous and courteous to officers, and men flocked to him.
units.literal: Emperor Wen then assigned many of his subordinates to Zigao; Zigao also was generous with wealth and courteous to officers; those who came to him were very numerous.

units.zh: 文帝嗣位，除右軍將軍。
units.en: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Han Zigao became General of the Right Army.
units.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne, Han Zigao was appointed General of the Right Army.

units.zh: 天嘉元年，封文招縣子，邑三百戶。
units.en: In Tianjia 1 (560), he was made Viscount of Wenzhao County with a three-hundred-household fief.
units.literal: In Tianjia 1, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Wenzhao County, with a fief of three hundred households.

units.zh: 王琳至于柵口，子高宿衛臺內。
units.en: When Wang Lin reached Zhankou, Zigao guarded the palace precincts.
units.literal: When Wang Lin reached Zhankou, Zigao served as guard inside the palace precinct.

units.zh: 及琳平，子高所統益多，將士依附之者，子高盡力論進，文帝皆任使焉。
units.en: After Wang Lin was pacified, Zigao's command grew. He strongly recommended the officers and soldiers who joined him, and Emperor Wen put them all to use.
units.literal: After Lin was pacified, those under Zigao's command increased; officers and soldiers who attached themselves to him were all earnestly recommended for advancement by Zigao, and Emperor Wen appointed and employed them all.

units.zh: 二年，遷員外散騎常侍、壯武將軍、成州刺史。
units.en: In the second year, he was promoted to Extra Regular Cavalier Attendant, General of Mighty Valor, and Inspector of Chengzhou.
units.literal: In the second year, he was transferred to Extra Regular Cavalier Attendant, General of Mighty Valor, and Inspector of Chengzhou.

units.zh: 及征留異，隨侯安都頓桃支嶺巖下。
units.en: During the campaign against Liu Yi, he accompanied Hou Andu and camped below Taozhi Ridge.
units.literal: When Liu Yi was campaigned against, he followed Hou Andu and encamped below the cliffs of Taozhi Ridge.

units.zh: 時子高兵甲精銳，別御一營，單馬入陳，傷項之左，一髻半落。
units.en: Zigao's troops were elite. Commanding a separate camp, he rode alone into the enemy line, where he was wounded on the left side of the neck and half his topknot was cut away.
units.literal: At the time Zigao's troops and armor were elite; he separately commanded one camp, rode alone into the enemy formation, was wounded on the left side of the neck, and half of his topknot was cut away.

units.zh: 異平，除假節、貞毅將軍、東陽太守。
units.en: After Liu Yi was pacified, he was appointed Acting with Staff, General of Resolute Constancy, and Administrator of Dongyang.
units.literal: After Yi was pacified, he was appointed Acting with Staff, General of Resolute Constancy, and Administrator of Dongyang.

units.zh: 五年，章昭達等自臨川征晉安，子高自安泉嶺會于建安，諸將中人馬最為彊盛。
units.en: In the fifth year, when Zhang Zhaoda and the others marched from Linchuan against Jin'an, Zigao came over Anquan Ridge to meet them at Jian'an; of all the generals, his men and horses were the strongest.
units.literal: In the fifth year, Zhang Zhaoda and others marched from Linchuan against Jin'an; Zigao came from Anquan Ridge to join them at Jian'an, and among the generals his men and horses were the strongest.

units.zh: 晉安平，以功遷通直散騎常侍，進爵為伯，增邑并前四百戶。
units.en: After Jin'an was pacified, he was promoted for merit to Cavalier Attendant for Direct Service, advanced to Earl, and received an additional four hundred households counting the previous grant.
units.literal: After Jin'an was pacified, for his merit he was promoted to Cavalier Attendant for Direct Service, advanced in noble rank to Earl, and his fief was increased, together with the former grant, by four hundred households.

units.zh: 六年，徵為右衛將軍，至都，鎮領軍府。
units.en: In the sixth year, he was summoned as General of the Right Guard and, on reaching the capital, took up station at the Leading Army headquarters.
units.literal: In the sixth year, he was summoned to be General of the Right Guard; upon reaching the capital, he took station at the Headquarters of the Leading Army.

units.zh: 文帝不豫，入侍醫藥。
units.en: When Emperor Wen fell ill, Zigao attended him and oversaw his medicines.
units.literal: When Emperor Wen was unwell, he entered to attend on his medicines.

units.zh: 廢帝即位，遷散騎常侍，右衛如故，移頓于新安寺。
units.en: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, Zigao became Cavalier Attendant while retaining the Right Guard post, and moved his quarters to Xin'an Monastery.
units.literal: When the Deposed Emperor ascended, he was transferred to Cavalier Attendant, with the Right Guard as before, and moved his station to Xin'an Monastery.

units.zh: 高宗入輔，子高兵權過重，深不自安，好參訪臺閣，又求出為衡、廣諸鎮。
units.en: When Emperor Xuan entered to govern, Zigao’s military power weighed too heavy. Uneasy, he frequented the Terrace offices and asked to be posted to Heng and Guang.
units.literal: When Emperor Xuan entered to assist in government, Zigao's military authority was excessive; he felt deeply ill at ease, liked to visit the Terrace offices, and also sought to go out to the garrisons of Heng and Guang.

units.zh: 光大元年八月，前上虞縣令陸昉及子高軍主告其謀反，高宗在尚書省，因召文武在位議立皇太子，子高預焉，平旦入省，執之，送廷尉，其夕與到仲舉同賜死，時年三十。
units.en: In the eighth month of Guangda year 1 (567), the former magistrate of Shangyu, Lu Fang, and one of Zigao’s army commanders reported a plot to rebel. Emperor Xuan was in the masters of writing office and called the officials to discuss the crown prince. Zigao came at dawn, was seized and sent to the court of trials, and that evening was granted death with Dao Zhongju. He was thirty.
units.literal: Eighth month, first year of Guangda: the former magistrate of Shangyu, Lu Fang, and Zigao's army commander reported his plotting rebellion. Emperor Xuan was in the Masters of Writing office and thereupon summoned civil and military officials in post to discuss establishing the crown prince. Zigao was among them; at dawn he entered the office, was seized, and sent to the Court of Trials. That evening he was granted death together with Dao Zhongju; he was thirty years old.

units.zh: 父延慶及子弟並原宥。
units.en: His father Yanqing and his brothers and sons were all pardoned.
units.literal: His father Yanqing and sons and younger brothers were all pardoned.

units.zh: 延慶因子高之寵，官至給事中、山陰令。
units.en: Through Zigao’s favor Yanqing rose to secretariat attendant and magistrate of Shanyin.
units.literal: Yanqing, because of Zigao's favor, reached Attendant of the Secretariat and Magistrate of Shanyin.

units.zh: 華皎，晉陵暨陽人。
units.en: Hua Jiao was from Jiyang in Jinling.
units.literal: Hua Jiao was a man of Jiyang in Jinling.

units.zh: 世為小吏。
units.en: His family had served for generations as minor officials.
units.literal: For generations his family had been minor officials.

units.zh: 皎，梁代為尚書比部令史。
units.en: Under Liang, Jiao served as a clerk in the Bibu section of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: During Liang, Jiao served as a clerk of the Bibu section of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 侯景之亂，事景黨王偉。
units.en: During Hou Jing's rebellion, he served Wang Wei, an associate of Jing.
units.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion, he served Wang Wei, one of Jing's faction.

units.zh: 高祖南下，文帝為景所囚，皎遇文帝甚厚。
units.en: When Gaozu marched south, Emperor Wen was being held by Jing, and Jiao treated him with great kindness.
units.literal: When Gaozu went south, Emperor Wen was held prisoner by Jing, and Jiao treated Emperor Wen very generously.

units.zh: 景平，文帝為吳興太守，以皎為都錄事，軍府穀帛，多以委之。
units.en: After Hou Jing was pacified, Emperor Wen became Administrator of Wuxing and made Jiao chief recorder, entrusting much of the military office's grain and silk to him.
units.literal: After Jing was pacified, Emperor Wen became Administrator of Wuxing and made Jiao chief recorder; much of the army office's grain and silk was entrusted to him.

units.zh: 皎聰慧，勤於簿領。
units.en: Jiao was intelligent and diligent in handling records and accounts.
units.literal: Jiao was intelligent and diligent with registers and accounts.

units.zh: 及文帝平杜龕，仍配以人馬甲仗，猶為都錄事。
units.en: When Emperor Wen pacified Du Kan, he assigned Jiao men, horses, armor, and weapons while keeping him as chief recorder.
units.literal: When Emperor Wen pacified Du Kan, he still assigned Jiao men, horses, armor, and weapons, and Jiao remained chief recorder.

units.zh: 御下分明，善於撫養。
units.en: He managed his subordinates with clarity and was good at looking after them.
units.literal: In governing subordinates he was clear and orderly, and was good at caring for and sustaining them.

units.zh: 時兵荒之後，百姓饑饉，皎解衣推食，多少必均，因稍擢為暨陽、山陰二縣令。
units.en: In the aftermath of war and famine, when the people were starving, Jiao shared out clothing and food evenly, and was gradually promoted to magistrate of Jiyang and Shanyin counties.
units.literal: At that time, after war and famine, the common people were hungry; Jiao shared clothing and food, making large and small portions equal, and was gradually promoted to magistrate of the two counties Jiyang and Shanyin.

units.zh: 文帝即位，除開遠將軍，左軍將軍。
units.en: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Jiao was appointed General Who Opens the Distant and General of the Left Army.
units.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, Jiao was appointed General Who Opens the Distant and General of the Left Army.

units.zh: 天嘉元年，封懷仁縣伯，邑四百戶。
units.en: In Tianjia 1 (560), he was made Earl of Huairen County with a four-hundred-household fief.
units.literal: In Tianjia 1, he was enfeoffed as Earl of Huairen County, with a fief of four hundred households.

units.zh: 王琳東下，皎隨侯瑱拒之。
units.en: When Wang Lin marched east, Jiao followed Hou Tian to resist him.
units.literal: Wang Lin marched east; Jiao followed Hou Tian to resist him.

units.zh: 琳平，鎮湓城，知江州事。
units.en: When Lin fell, Jiao garrisoned Pen city and ran Jiangzhou affairs.
units.literal: When Lin was pacified, [Jiao] garrisoned Pen city and oversaw Jiangzhou affairs.

units.zh: 時南州守宰多鄉里酋豪，不遵朝憲，文帝令皎以法馭之。
units.en: Southern prefects and magistrates were often local strongmen who ignored the court. Emperor Wen ordered Jiao to bring them to heel by law.
units.literal: At that time the prefects and magistrates of the southern provinces were mostly local chieftains and strongmen who did not obey court law; Emperor Wen ordered Jiao to rein them in by law.

units.zh: 王琳奔散，將卒多附於皎。
units.en: When Wang Lin’s army broke up, his officers and men mostly joined Jiao.
units.literal: When Wang Lin was routed and scattered, generals and soldiers mostly attached themselves to Jiao.

units.zh: 三年，除假節、通直散騎常侍、仁武將軍、新州刺史資，監江州。
units.en: In the third year he was given provisional credentials, direct-communication regular attendant, benevolent and martial general, and inspector of Xinzhou’s salary while supervising Jiangzhou.
units.literal: In the third year he was appointed provisional credentials, Regular Attendant Direct Communication, Benevolent and Martial General, and salary as Inspector of Xinzhou, supervising Jiangzhou.

units.zh: 尋詔督尋陽太原高唐南北新蔡五郡諸軍事、尋陽太守，假節、將軍、州資、監如故。
units.en: Soon he was ordered to command armies in Xunyang, Taiyuan, Gaotang, and North and South Xincai and was made administrator of Xunyang, keeping his credentials, general’s title, salary, and supervision.
units.literal: Soon an edict ordered him to supervise military affairs in the five commanderies of Xunyang, Taiyuan, Gaotang, South and North Xincai, and made him Administrator of Xunyang; provisional credentials, general, provincial salary, and supervision remained as before.

units.zh: 周迪謀反，遣其兄子伏甲於船中，偽稱賈人，欲於湓城襲皎。
units.en: Zhou Di rebelled and sent his nephew with hidden troops aboard ship, posing as merchants, to strike Jiao at Pen city.
units.literal: Zhou Di plotted rebellion and sent his elder brother's son to lie in ambush aboard ship, falsely claiming to be merchants, intending to strike Jiao at Pen city.

units.zh: 未發，事覺，皎遣人逆擊之，盡獲其船仗。
units.en: Before they moved, the plot was found out. Jiao sent men against them and took all their ships and weapons.
units.literal: Before it was launched the affair was discovered; Jiao sent men to intercept them and seized all their ships and arms.

units.zh: 其年，皎隨都督吳明徹征迪，迪平，以功授散騎常侍、平南將軍、臨川太守，進爵為侯，增封并前五百戶。
units.en: That year Jiao followed area commander Wu Mingche against Di. When Di fell, he was made regular attendant, general who pacifies the south, and administrator of Linchuan, raised to marquis with five hundred households in all.
units.literal: That year Jiao followed Area Commander Wu Mingche to campaign against Di; when Di was pacified, by merit he was appointed Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the South, and Administrator of Linchuan, advanced in rank to marquis, his fief increased together with the previous to five hundred households.

units.zh: 未拜，入朝，仍授使持節、都督湘巴等四州諸軍事、湘州刺史，常侍、將軍如故。
units.en: Before he took office he went to court and was given credentials as area commander over Xiang, Ba, and the other provinces and made inspector of Xiangzhou, retaining his attendant and general titles.
units.literal: Before he took up the appointment he entered court and was thereupon given credentials, made Area Commander over military affairs in the four provinces of Xiang, Ba, and others, and Inspector of Xiangzhou; regular attendant and general remained as before.

units.zh: 皎起自下吏，善營產業，湘川地多所出，所得並入朝廷，糧運竹木，委輸甚眾；
units.en: Jiao rose from a petty clerk and knew how to build wealth. The Xiang region yields much, and he sent it all to court—grain, bamboo, timber, and convoys beyond count;
units.literal: Jiao rose from a low clerk, was skilled at managing property; the lands of the Xiang river region produce much, and what he obtained all entered the court—grain transport, bamboo and timber, the deliveries entrusted were very numerous;

units.zh: 至于油蜜脯菜之屬，莫不營辦。
units.en: As for oil, honey, cured meats, and vegetables—nothing was left unprovided.
units.literal: as for oil, honey, dried meats, vegetables, and the like, there was nothing he did not supply.

units.zh: 又征伐川洞，多致銅鼓、生口，並送于京師。
units.en: He also fought the hill peoples and sent bronze drums and captives to the capital in great numbers.
units.literal: He also campaigned in the river valleys and cave settlements and brought in many bronze drums and captives, all sent to the capital.

units.zh: 廢帝即位，進號安南將軍，改封重安縣侯，[4]食邑一千五百戶。
units.en: When the Deposed Emperor succeeded, Jiao was made general who pacifies the south and re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Chong’an [4] with one thousand five hundred households.
units.literal: When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne, [Jiao's] title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the South, his enfeoffment changed to Marquis of Chong'an county, fief one thousand five hundred households.

units.zh: 文帝以湘州出杉木舟，使皎營造大艦金翅等二百餘艘，并諸水戰之具，欲以入漢及峽。
units.en: Emperor Wen, since Xiangzhou furnished fir for ships, ordered Jiao to build more than two hundred Golden-Wing great ships and all river-war gear, intending to enter the Han and the gorges.
units.literal: Emperor Wen, because Xiangzhou produced fir timber for boats, ordered Jiao to build more than two hundred great ships of the Golden-Wing type and all equipment for river warfare, intending to enter the Han and the Gorges.

units.zh: 韓子高誅後，皎內不自安，繕甲聚徒，厚禮所部守宰。
units.en: After Zigao’s death Jiao grew uneasy, armored men and gathered followers, and lavished gifts on his subordinate officials.
units.literal: After Han Zigao was executed, Jiao felt ill at ease within and repaired armor and gathered followers, treating the prefects and magistrates under him with lavish courtesy.

units.zh: 高宗頻命皎送大艦金翅等，推遷不至。
units.en: Emperor Xuan repeatedly ordered him to send the Golden-Wing great ships. Jiao stalled and would not deliver.
units.literal: Emperor Xuan repeatedly ordered Jiao to send the great Golden-Wing ships and the like; he put off and delayed and did not arrive.

units.zh: 光大元年，密啟求廣州，以觀時主意，高宗偽許之，而詔書未出。
units.en: In the first year of Guangda (567) he secretly asked for Guangzhou to test the court’s mind. Emperor Xuan pretended to agree, but no edict had yet gone out.
units.literal: In the first year of Guangda he secretly memorialized asking for Guangzhou to observe the court's intent; Emperor Xuan falsely assented, but the edict had not yet been issued.

units.zh: 皎亦遣使句引周兵，又崇奉蕭巋為主，士馬甚盛。
units.en: Jiao also sent envoys to draw in Northern Zhou troops and set up Xiao Kui as his sovereign. His army grew very large.
units.literal: Jiao also sent envoys to draw in Northern Zhou troops and further honored Xiao Kui as sovereign; his warriors and horses were very numerous.

units.zh: 詔乃以吳明徹為湘州刺史，實欲以輕兵襲之。
units.en: An edict then named Wu Mingche inspector of Xiangzhou, intending in truth to strike Jiao with a light force.
units.literal: An edict then made Wu Mingche Inspector of Xiangzhou, in fact intending to strike him with light troops.

units.zh: 是時慮皎先發，乃前遣明徹率眾三萬，乘金翅直趨郢州，又遣撫軍大將軍淳于量率眾五萬，乘大艦以繼之，又令假節、冠武將軍楊文通別從安
units.en: Fearing Jiao would move first, they sent Mingche with thirty thousand men in Golden-Wing ships straight for Yingzhou, and pacifying-the-army grand general Chunyu Liang with fifty thousand in great ships behind him, and ordered provisional-credentials crowned-with-martiality general Yang Wentong by a separate route from An
units.literal: At that time, fearing Jiao would strike first, they first sent Mingche at the head of thirty thousand men, riding Golden-Wing [ships] straight for Yingzhou, and also sent Pacifying-the-Army Grand General Chunyu Liang at the head of fifty thousand men, riding great ships to follow after, and also ordered Provisional Credentials, Crowned-with-Martiality General Yang Wentong to set out separately from An

units.en: (Cheng)
units.literal: (Cheng)

units.zh: 成步道出茶陵，[5]又令巴山太守黃法慧別從宜陽出澧陵，往掩襲，出其不意，并與江州刺史章昭達、郢州刺史程靈洗等參謀討賊。
units.en: Cheng by the foot-path through Chaling, [5] and ordered Bashan administrator Huang Fahui from Yiyang through Liling for a surprise blow, together with Jiangzhou inspector Zhang Zhaoda, Yingzhou inspector Cheng Lingxi, and others to plan the suppression.
units.literal: Cheng by the foot-path out through Chaling, and also ordered Administrator of Bashan Huang Fahui to set out separately from Yiyang through Liling to make a surprise attack, taking him unawares, and together with Inspector of Jiangzhou Zhang Zhaoda, Inspector of Yingzhou Cheng Lingxi, and others to consult on suppressing the rebel.

units.zh: 是時蕭巋遣水軍為皎聲援。
units.en: Xiao Kui then sent a river fleet to support Jiao.
units.literal: At that time Xiao Kui sent a river fleet to support Jiao.

units.zh: 周武又遣其弟衛國公宇文直率眾屯魯山，又遣其柱國長胡公拓跋定人馬三萬，攻圍郢州。
units.en: Emperor Wu of Zhou also sent his brother the Duke of Weiguo, Yuwen Zhi, to camp at Lushan, and his pillar of state Tuoba Ding with thirty thousand troops to besiege Yingzhou.
units.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou also sent his younger brother the Duke of Weiguo, Yuwen Zhi, at the head of troops garrisoned at Lushan, and also sent his Pillar of State the Duke of Chang, Tuoba Ding, with thirty thousand men and horses to attack and besiege Yingzhou.

units.zh: 蕭巋授皎司空，巴州刺史戴僧朔，衡陽內史任蠻奴，巴陵內史潘智虔，岳陽太守章昭裕，
units.en: Xiao Kui made Jiao minister of works and set Dai Sengshuo over Ba, Ren Mannu over Hengyang, Pan Zhiquan over Baling, and Zhang Zhaoyu over Yueyang;
units.literal: Xiao Kui appointed Jiao Minister of Works; Dai Sengshuo, Administrator of Ba; Ren Mannu, Interior Minister of Hengyang; Pan Zhiquan, Interior Minister of Baling; Zhang Zhaoyu, Administrator of Yueyang;

units.en: (Du)
units.literal: (Du)

units.zh: 桂陽太守曹宣，[6]湘東太守錢明，並隸於皎。
units.en: Guiyang administrator Cao Xuan, [6] Xiangdong administrator Qian Ming, and others—all under Jiao’s command.
units.literal: Guiyang Administrator Cao Xuan, Administrator of Xiangdong Qian Ming, and all were placed under Jiao.

units.zh: 又長沙太守曹慶等本隸皎下，因為之用。
units.en: Changsha administrator Cao Qing and others had already been Jiao’s men and now served him.
units.literal: Also Administrator of Changsha Cao Qing and others had originally been under Jiao and therefore served his use.

units.zh: 帝恐上流宰守並為皎扇惑，乃下詔曰：「賊皎輿皂微賤，特逢獎擢，任據藩牧，屬當寵寄，背斯造育，興構姦謀，樹立蕭氏，盟約彰露，鴆毒存心，志危宗社，扇結邊境，驅逼士庶，蟻聚巴、湘，豕突鄢、郢，逆天反地，人神忿嫉。
units.en: The emperor feared upstream governors would side with Jiao and issued an edict: “The traitor Jiao rose from cart and stable. Promoted by chance to a frontier post, he should have been grateful. Instead he rebelled, enthroned the Xiao line, sealed open pacts, and aimed at the dynasty. He stirred the borders, drove the people, swarmed Ba and Xiang like ants, and charged Yan and Ying like boars—heaven and earth alike revile him.
units.literal: The Emperor feared that the officials commanding the upper Yangtze would all be swayed by Jiao, and thereupon issued an edict saying: "The rebel Jiao is of cart-and-servant mean birth; he happened to meet with reward and promotion, was entrusted with a frontier post and ought to have received favored care, yet he turned against what nurtured him and raised treacherous plots, set up the Xiao house, their covenant and pact plain to see, poison and malice in his heart, his aim to endanger the altars of state, inciting the border regions, driving and pressing scholars and commoners, ants massed in Ba and Xiang, pigs charging at Yan and Ying, opposing Heaven and turning against earth—men and spirits alike rage.

units.zh: 征南將軍量、安南將軍明徹、郢州刺史靈洗，受律專征，備盡心力，撫勞驍雄，舟師俱進，義烈爭奮，凶惡奔殄，獻捷相望，重氛載廓，言念泣罪，思與惟新。
units.en: Campaigning-south general Liang, pacifying-south general Mingche, and Yingzhou inspector Lingxi took the law and marched with all their strength, heartening the brave as the fleets advanced together. Valor flared, the wicked were crushed, victory reports came in waves, and the foul air cleared. In judging guilt I look to renewal.
units.literal: Campaigning-South General Liang, Pacifying-South General Mingche, and Inspector of Yingzhou Lingxi received the law and led the dedicated campaign, exhausting mind and strength, comforting and encouraging the fierce and heroic; the river forces advanced together; righteous valor vied in ardor; the vicious and wicked ran to destruction; reports of victory came one after another; heavy miasma was cleared away again and again. Speaking of weeping over guilt, We think of renewal.

units.zh: 可曲赦湘、巴二州：凡厥為賊所逼制，預在凶黨，悉皆不問；
units.en: Let Xiang and Ba be partly pardoned: all who were forced into the rebel ranks and joined the guilty faction shall go unquestioned;
units.literal: A partial pardon may be granted to the two provinces of Xiang and Ba: all who were compelled by the rebels and took part in the wicked faction are wholly not to be questioned;

units.zh: 其賊主帥節
units.en: their rebel chieftains, commanders, and
units.literal: their rebel chieftains', commanders', and

units.en: (xiang)
units.literal: (xiang)

units.zh: 將，[7]並許開恩出首，一同曠蕩。」
units.en: generals [7] may all surrender with clemency and share in a general amnesty."
units.literal: jiang, [7] all are permitted to turn themselves in with grace and receive a general pardon together."

units.zh: 先是，詔又遣司空徐度與楊文通等自安成步出湘東，以襲皎後。
units.en: Earlier an edict had also sent Xu Du, minister of works, with Yang Wentong and others out from Ancheng overland through eastern Xiang to hit Jiao from behind.
units.literal: Earlier, an edict had also sent Minister of Works Xu Du with Yang Wentong and others to march out from Ancheng by land route into eastern Xiang to strike Jiao from the rear.

units.zh: 時皎陣于巴州之白螺，列舟艦與王師相持未決。
units.en: Jiao then held his line at White Snail in Ba commandery, his ships drawn up against the imperial fleet in an unresolved standoff.
units.literal: At that time Jiao had drawn up his battle line at White Snail in Ba commandery, arraying his fleet to face the royal army in stalemate without decision.

units.zh: 及聞徐度趨湘州，乃率兵自巴、郢因便風下戰。
units.en: Learning that Xu Du was marching on Xiangzhou, he took his army down from Ba and Ying with a fair wind and joined battle.
units.literal: When he heard that Xu Du was pressing toward Xiangzhou, he then led his troops down from Ba and Ying with a favoring wind to give battle.

units.zh: 淳于量、吳明徹等募軍中小艦，多賞金銀，令先出當賊大艦，受其拍。
units.en: Chunyu Liang and Wu Mingche raised small boats from the ranks, paid them well in gold and silver, and sent them out first to take the enemy great ships' ramming blows.
units.literal: Chunyu Liang, Wu Mingche, and others recruited small boats from among the troops, richly rewarded them with gold and silver, and ordered them out first to meet the rebels' great ships and take their ramming blows.

units.zh: 賊艦發拍皆盡，然後官軍以大艦拍之，賊艦皆碎，沒于中流。
units.en: Once the rebel ships had spent their rams, the imperial great ships rammed them; every rebel vessel was broken and went down mid-river.
units.literal: When the rebel ships had exhausted all their rams, the government forces then struck them with great ships; the rebel ships were all smashed and sank in midstream.

units.zh: 賊又以大艦載薪，因風放火，俄而風轉自焚，賊軍大敗。
units.en: The rebels then packed great ships with fuel and tried to burn the fleet downwind; the wind swung back and set their own ships ablaze, and they were routed.
units.literal: The rebels again loaded great ships with firewood and, riding the wind, set fire; soon the wind turned and burned them instead, and the rebel army suffered a great defeat.

units.zh: 皎乃與戴僧朔單舸走，過巴陵，不敢登城，徑奔江陵。
units.en: Jiao fled with Dai Sengshuo in one boat; at Baling he dared not enter the walls and ran straight for Jiangling.
units.literal: Jiao then fled with Dai Sengshuo in a single boat; passing Baling he did not dare enter the city and went straight to Jiangling.

units.zh: 拓跋定等無復船渡，步趨巴陵，巴陵城邑為官軍所據，乃向湘州。
units.en: Tuoba Ding and his men had no ships to cross with and marched on Baling on foot; the Baling towns were already in imperial hands, so they headed for Xiangzhou.
units.literal: Tuoba Ding and the others had no boats left to cross; they went on foot toward Baling, but the walled towns of Baling were already held by the government army, so they turned toward Xiangzhou.

units.zh: 至水口，不得濟，食且盡，詣軍請降。
units.en: At the river mouth they could not get across; with provisions almost gone they came in and surrendered.
units.literal: Reaching the river mouth they could not cross; their food was nearly gone, and they came to the army to surrender.

units.zh: 俘獲萬餘人，馬四千餘匹，送于京師。
units.en: More than ten thousand prisoners and four thousand-odd horses were sent to the capital.
units.literal: More than ten thousand were captured, with over four thousand horses, and sent to the capital.

units.zh: 皎黨曹慶、錢明、潘智虔、魯閑、席慧略等四十餘人並誅，唯任蠻奴、章昭裕、曹宣、劉廣業獲免。
units.en: Jiao's followers Cao Qing, Qian Ming, Pan Zhiquan, Lu Xian, Xi Huilüe, and more than forty others were put to death; only Ren Mannu, Zhang Zhaoyu, Cao Xuan, and Liu Guangye were pardoned.
units.literal: Jiao's partisans Cao Qing, Qian Ming, Pan Zhiquan, Lu Xian, Xi Huilüe, and more than forty others were all executed; only Ren Mannu, Zhang Zhaoyu, Cao Xuan, and Liu Guangye were spared.

units.zh: 戴僧朔，吳郡錢塘人也。
units.en: Dai Sengshuo was from Qiantang in Wu commandery.
units.literal: Dai Sengshuo was a man of Qiantang in Wu commandery.

units.zh: 有膂力，勇健善戰，族兄右將軍僧錫甚愛之。
units.en: Powerful, bold, and a capable fighter, he was much favored by his kinsman Sengxi, right general.
units.literal: He had physical strength, was brave and skilled in battle, and his clansman the Right General Sengxi greatly loved him.

units.zh: 僧錫年老，征討恆使僧朔領眾。
units.en: As Sengxi aged, he regularly put Sengshuo in command on campaign.
units.literal: When Sengxi grew old, on campaigns he always had Sengshuo lead the troops.

units.zh: 平王琳有功。
units.en: He earned merit in the campaign that pacified Wang Lin.
units.literal: He had merit in pacifying Wang Lin.

units.zh: 僧錫卒，仍代為南丹陽太守，鎮採石。
units.en: After Sengxi's death he replaced him as administrator of South Danyang and held Caishi.
units.literal: When Sengxi died, he succeeded him as Administrator of South Danyang and garrisoned at Caishi.

units.zh: 從征留異，侯安都於巖下出戰，為賊斫傷，僧朔單刀步援。
units.en: Campaigning against Liu Yi, Hou Andu fought the enemy below the cliff and was wounded; Sengshuo went in alone on foot with one sword to pull him out.
units.literal: On the campaign against Liu Yi, Hou Andu came out to fight from below the cliff and was cut down by the rebels; Sengshuo went on foot alone with a single blade to rescue him.

units.zh: 以功除壯武將軍、北江州刺史，領南陵太守。
units.en: For this he was made trustworthy-martial general and inspector of North Jiangzhou, and also administrator of Nanling.
units.literal: For his merit he was made Trustworthy Martial General and Inspector of North Jiangzhou, holding concurrently the post of Administrator of Nanling.

units.zh: 又從征周迪有功，遷巴州刺史，假節、將軍如故。
units.en: He campaigned again against Zhou Di with merit, was moved to administrator of Ba commandery, and kept his staff and general's rank.
units.literal: He again followed on the campaign against Zhou Di with merit, was transferred to Administrator of Ba commandery, and his credentials and general's title remained as before.

units.zh: 至是同皎為逆，伏誅於江陵。
units.en: He then rebelled with Jiao and was executed at Jiangling.
units.literal: At this time he joined Jiao in rebellion and was executed at Jiangling.

units.zh: 曹慶本王琳將，蕭莊偽署左衛將軍、吳州刺史，部領亞於潘純陀。
units.en: Cao Qing had been one of Wang Lin's generals; the puppet ruler Xiao Zhuang made him left guard general and inspector of Wu commandery, ranking below Pan Chuntuo.
units.literal: Cao Qing had originally been a Wang Lin general; Xiao Zhuang falsely appointed him Left Guard General and Inspector of Wu commandery, and his command ranked below Pan Chuntuo's.

units.zh: 琳敗，文帝以配皎，官至長沙太守。
units.en: After Lin's defeat Emperor Wen placed him under Jiao; he rose to administrator of Changsha.
units.literal: When Lin was defeated, Emperor Wen assigned him to Jiao; he rose to Administrator of Changsha.

units.zh: 錢明，本高祖主帥，後歷湘州諸郡守。
units.en: Qian Ming had once been a chief commander under the Founder and later held several posts as prefect in the Xiang region.
units.literal: Qian Ming had originally been a chief commander under the Founder; afterward he successively held governorships in the Xiang region.

units.zh: 潘智虔，純陀之子，少有志氣，年二十為巴陵內史。
units.en: Pan Zhiquan was Chuntuo's son—spirited from youth and made inner administrator of Baling at twenty.
units.literal: Pan Zhiquan was Chuntuo's son; from youth he had ambition and resolve, and at twenty he became Inner Administrator of Baling.

units.zh: 魯閑，吳郡錢塘人。
units.en: Lu Xian was from Qiantang in Wu commandery.
units.literal: Lu Xian was a man of Qiantang in Wu commandery.

units.zh: 席慧略，安定人。
units.en: Xi Huilüe was from Anding.
units.literal: Xi Huilüe was a man of Anding.

units.zh: 閑本張彪主帥，慧略王琳部下，文帝皆配于皎，官至郡守。
units.en: Xian had served Zhang Biao as chief commander and Huilüe had been under Wang Lin; Emperor Wen gave both to Jiao, and each became a commandery governor.
units.literal: Xian had originally been a Zhang Biao chief commander, and Huilüe a Wang Lin subordinate; Emperor Wen assigned both to Jiao, and each rose to a commandery governorship.

units.zh: 並伏誅。
units.en: All were put to death.
units.literal: All were executed.

units.zh: 章昭裕，昭達之弟；
units.en: Zhang Zhaoyu was Zhaoda's younger brother;
units.literal: Zhang Zhaoyu was Zhaoda's younger brother;

units.zh: 劉廣業，廣德之弟；
units.en: Liu Guangye was Guangde's younger brother;
units.literal: Liu Guangye was Guangde's younger brother;

units.zh: 曹宣，高祖舊臣；
units.en: Cao Xuan was an old minister of the Founder;
units.literal: Cao Xuan was an old minister of the Founder;

units.zh: 任蠻奴嘗有密啟於朝廷；
units.en: Ren Mannu had once sent a secret memorial to the court;
units.literal: Ren Mannu had once sent a secret memorial to the court;

units.zh: 由是並獲宥。
units.en: for which they were all spared.
units.literal: for this reason they all received pardon.

units.zh: 史臣曰：韓子高、華皎雖復瓶筲小器，輿臺末品，文帝鑒往古之得人，救當今之急弊，達聰明目之術，安黎和眾之宜，寄以腹心，不論冑閥。
units.en: The historian writes: Han Zigao and Hua Jiao were trifling men of humble birth, yet Emperor Wen—seeing how past ages chose talent and how pressing his own troubles were—used sharp judgment and policies that calmed the realm, and gave them his full trust without asking after their pedigrees.
units.literal: The historian says: Although Han Zigao and Hua Jiao were but petty vessels and the lowest ranks of servitors, Emperor Wen, discerning how the ancients gained men and remedying the urgent ills of his own day, applied the art of keen sight and clear hearing and the policy of settling the people and harmonizing the masses—entrusting them with his inmost counsel without regard to pedigree.

units.zh: 皎早參近昵，[8]嘗預艱虞，知其無隱，賞以悉力，有見信之誠，非可疑之地。
units.en: Jiao had long served him closely [8], had shared danger, and showed he had nothing to hide; the emperor repaid him with full trust—grounds for confidence, not for doubt.
units.literal: Jiao early took part in intimate service, [8] once shared in hardship and peril; [the emperor] knew that he had nothing to hide and rewarded him for exerting his full strength—there was the sincerity of one trusted, not ground for suspicion.

units.zh: 皎據有上游，忠於文帝。
units.en: Jiao held the upper river and had been loyal to Emperor Wen.
units.literal: Jiao held the upper Yangtze and was loyal to Emperor Wen.

units.zh: 仲舉、子高亦無爽於臣節者矣。
units.en: Dao Zhongju and Zigao, too, had not failed in subject's duty.
units.literal: Dao Zhongju and Zigao likewise did not fall short in the duty of a subject.

units.zh: 博士到洽議曰：「周郎年未弱冠，便自講一經，雖曰諸生，實堪師表，無俟策試。」
units.en: Doctor Dao Qia argued, "Young Zhou is not yet twenty yet already teaches a classic himself. Though called a student, he is fit to be a teacher. There is no need for a written examination."
units.literal: Doctor Dao Qia deliberated and said, "Master Zhou is not yet of weak-crown age yet already expounds a classic himself; though called a student, he is truly fit to be a teacher and model—there is no need to wait for a written examination."

units.zh: 吏部尚書袁樞為尚書左僕射；
units.en: Yuan Shu, minister of personnel, became left vice director of the Masters of Writing;
units.literal: Minister of Personnel Yuan Shu became Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing;

units.zh: 光大元年春正月癸酉，尚書左僕射袁樞卒。
units.en: On guiyou day of the first month in Guangda year 1, Yuan Shu, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, died.
units.literal: On guiyou day of the first month, spring, in the first year of Guangda, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Shu died.

units.zh: 及世祖討彪，彪將沈泰、吳寶真、申縉等皆降，而子隆力戰敗績，世祖義之，復使領其部曲，板為中兵參軍。
units.en: When Emperor Wen moved against Biao, Biao's generals Shen Tai, Wu Baozhen, Shen Jin, and the rest surrendered—but Zilong fought on and lost. Emperor Wen admired his constancy, restored him to his old troops, and brevetted him military adjutant of the central guard.
units.literal: When Emperor Wen campaigned against Biao, Biao's generals Shen Tai, Wu Baozhen, Shen Jin, and others all surrendered, but Zilong fought hard and was defeated; Emperor Wen honored his loyalty, had him again lead his old command, and commissioned him military adjutant of the central guard.

units.zh: 王琳遣其將常眾愛、曹慶率兵援余孝勱。
units.en: Wang Lin sent his generals Chang Zhong'ai and Cao Qing with troops to support Yu Xiaoqing.
units.literal: Wang Lin sent his generals Chang Zhong'ai and Cao Qing leading troops to aid Yu Xiaoqing.

units.zh: 六月戊子，儀同侯安都敗眾愛等於左里，獲琳從弟襲、主帥羊暕等三十餘人，眾愛遁走，庚寅，廬山民斬之，傳首京師。
units.en: In the sixth month, on wuzi day, Hou Andu, bearer of staff equal to the three dukes, routed Zhong'ai at Zuoli and took Wang Lin's cousin Xi, the commander Yang Xian, and more than thirty others. Zhong'ai fled; on gengyin day the people of Lushan killed him and sent his head to the capital.
units.literal: In the sixth month, on wuzi day, Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes Hou Andu defeated Zhong'ai and the others at Zuoli, capturing Wang Lin's younger cousin Xi, chief commander Yang Xian, and more than thirty others. Zhong'ai fled; on gengyin day the people of Lushan beheaded him and sent his head to the capital.

units.zh: 不佞素以名節自立，又受委東宮，乃與僕射到仲舉、中書舍人劉師知、尚書右丞王暹等，謀矯詔出高宗。
units.en: Buning had always stood on his reputation for integrity and had again been entrusted by the eastern palace. He therefore joined vice director Dao Zhongju, Secretariat attendant Liu Shizhi, right vice director Wang Xian, and others in plotting to forge an edict removing Emperor Xuan.
units.literal: Buning had always stood on his reputation for integrity and had again been entrusted by the Eastern Palace. He therefore joined Vice Director Dao Zhongju, Secretariat attendant Liu Shizhi, right vice director Wang Xian, and others in plotting to forge an edict removing Emperor Xuan.

units.zh: 及事發，仲舉等皆伏誅，高宗雅重不佞，特赦之，免其官而已。
units.en: When the affair broke, Zhongju and the rest were all executed. Emperor Xuan had long valued Buning and specially pardoned him, merely stripping his office.
units.literal: When the affair broke, Zhongju and the rest were all executed. Emperor Xuan had long valued Buning and specially pardoned him, merely stripping his office.

units.zh: 二月辛酉，以平西將軍、桂州刺史淳于量為開府儀同三司，進號鎮西大將軍。
units.en: In the second month, on xinyou day, Chunyu Liang, general who pacifies the west and inspector of Guizhou, was made grand mentor with staff and promoted to grand general who guards the west.
units.literal: In the second month, on xinyou day, the General Who Pacifies the West and Guizhou Inspector Chunyu Liang was made Grand Mentor with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes and promoted to Grand General Who Guards the West.

units.zh: 天嘉二年，除貞毅將軍、新安太守，仍隨侯安都東討留異。
units.en: In the second year of Tianjia (561) he was made steadfast-resolution general and administrator of Xin'an, and marched east with Hou Andu against Liu Yi.
units.literal: In the second year of Tianjia he was made Steadfast Resolution General and Administrator of Xin'an, and still followed Hou Andu east against Liu Yi.

units.zh: 異黨向文政據有新安，文季率精甲三百，輕往攻之。
units.en: Yi's man Xiang Wenzheng held Xin'an. Wenji took three hundred picked armored men and struck lightly.
units.literal: Yi's partisan Xiang Wenzheng held Xin'an; Wenji led three hundred picked armored men and went lightly to attack him.

units.zh: 四年，陳寶應與留異連結，又遣兵隨周迪更出臨川，世祖遣信義太守余孝頃自海道襲晉安，文季為之前軍，所向克捷。
units.en: In the fourth year Chen Baoying allied with Liu Yi and sent troops with Zhou Di against Linchuan again. Emperor Wen sent Yu Xiaoqing, administrator of Xinyi, by sea against Jin'an with Wenji as vanguard. Everywhere they went they prevailed.
units.literal: In the fourth year Chen Baoying joined with Liu Yi; he also sent troops with Zhou Di to come out again at Linchuan; Emperor Wen sent the Administrator of Xinyi, Yu Xiaoqing, by the sea route to strike Jin'an; Wenji served as his vanguard; wherever he went he won.

units.zh: 但靈洗之立功扞禦，久而見思，文季之埋魂異域，有足可憫。
units.en: Lingxi's defensive service is long missed; Wenji lies abroad, which moves deep pity.
units.literal: Yet Lingxi's merits in defense are long remembered with longing; Wenji's soul buried in a foreign land is greatly to be pitied.

units.zh: 孝珩破宇文邕，遂至長安，反時何與國家事。
units.en: If Xiaoheng defeats Yuwen Yong and then reaches Chang'an, what will rebellion have to do with the affairs of the state?
units.literal: If Xiaoheng defeats Yuwen Yong and then reaches Chang'an, what will rebellion have to do with the affairs of the state?

units.zh: 後周武帝在雲陽，宴齊君臣，自彈胡琵琶，命孝珩吹笛。
units.en: Later, when Emperor Wu of Zhou was at Yunyang, he feasted the Qi ruler and ministers, himself playing the barbarian pipa and ordering Xiaoheng to play the flute.
units.literal: Later, when Emperor Wu of Zhou was at Yunyang, he feasted the Qi ruler and ministers, himself playing the barbarian pipa and ordering Xiaoheng to play the flute.

units.zh: 固命之，舉笛裁至口，淚下嗚咽，武帝乃止。
units.en: Though pressed he obeyed; he raised the flute barely to his lips, tears falling in sobs, and Emperor Wu then stopped.
units.literal: Though pressed he obeyed; he raised the flute barely to his lips, tears falling in sobs, and Emperor Wu then stopped.

units.zh: 皎平，明徹於軍中輒戮安成內史楊文通，又受降人馬仗有不分明，景歷又坐不能匡正，被收付治。
units.en: When Jiao was pacified, Mingche on his own authority executed Yang Wentong, Interior Administrator of Ancheng, in camp and accepted surrendered personnel, horses, and weapons without clear division; Jingli was again charged for failing to correct this and was arrested for trial.
units.literal: When Jiao was pacified, Mingche on his own authority executed Interior Administrator of Ancheng Yang Wentong in the army, and again accepted surrendered men, horses, and weapons without clear division; Jingli again was charged for failing to correct this and was arrested and handed over for trial.

units.zh: 江南渠帥熊曇朗、周迪懷貳，琳遣李孝欽、樊猛與余孝頃同討之。
units.en: The channel lords of Jiangnan, Xiong Tanlang and Zhou Di, wavered in loyalty; Lin sent Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoxiang together to attack them.
units.literal: The channel lords of Jiangnan, Xiong Tanlang and Zhou Di, wavered in loyalty; Lin sent Li Xiaoqin, Fan Meng, and Yu Xiaoxiang together to attack them.

units.zh: 三將軍敗，並為敵所囚。
units.en: All three generals were defeated and taken prisoner by the enemy.
units.literal: All three generals were defeated and taken prisoner by the enemy.

units.zh: [10]雲麾將軍、郢州刺史程靈洗進號安西將軍。
units.en: Cheng Lingxi, cloud-banner general and inspector of Yingzhou, was promoted to general who pacifies the west.
units.literal: Cloud-Banner General and Inspector of Yingzhou Cheng Lingxi was advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the West.

units.zh: 仲威從弟廣德，亦好學，負才任氣。
units.en: Zhongwei's younger cousin Guangde also loved learning and was confident in his talent and spirit.
units.literal: Zhongwei's younger cousin Guangde also loved learning and relied on his talent and spirit.

units.zh: 廣德，承聖中以軍功官至給事黃門侍郎、湘東太守。
units.en: During Chengsheng, Guangde rose through military merit to attendant gentleman of the yellow gate and administrator of Xiangdong.
units.literal: During Chengsheng, Guangde rose through military merit to attendant gentleman of the yellow gate and administrator of Xiangdong.

units.zh: 光大中，假節、員外散騎常侍、雲旗將軍、河東太守。
units.en: During Guangda he became acting credential-holder, supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, cloud-banner general, and administrator of Hedong.
units.literal: During Guangda he was acting credential-holder, supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, cloud-banner general, and administrator of Hedong.

units.zh: 父之亨，梁安西湘東王長史、南郡太守。
units.en: His father Zhiheng was chief clerk to Liang's Prince of Xiangdong, general who secures the west, and administrator of Nanjun.
units.literal: His father Zhiheng was chief clerk to Liang's Prince of Xiangdong, general who secures the west, and administrator of Nanjun.

units.zh: 太建元年卒於郡，時年四十三，贈左衛將軍。
units.en: In Taijian year 1 (569), he died in the commandery, aged forty-three, and was posthumously made left guard general.
units.literal: In Taijian year 1 he died in the commandery, aged forty-three, and was posthumously presented as left guard general.

units.zh: 琳平，文帝以廣德為寧遠始興王府限外記室參軍，仍領其舊兵。
units.en: After Lin was pacified, Emperor Wen made Guangde extra-allowance records aide in the household of the Prince of Shixing, general who pacifies the distant, while letting him continue to command his old troops.
units.literal: When Lin was pacified, Emperor Wen made Guangde extra-allowance records aide in the household of the Prince of Shixing, general who pacifies the distant, and let him continue to command his old troops.

units.zh: 韓子高小豎輕佻，推心委仗，陰謀禍亂，決起蕭牆。
units.en: Han Ziga, a low creature, was light and reckless; the emperor trusted him with his heart, and treason brewed inside the palace.
units.literal: Han Ziga, a petty fellow, was frivolous and rash; the emperor gave him his inmost trust and relied on him, and secret plots for calamity rose within the palace walls.
